title: Add optional MON tools preview on frozen N-F 0.3.0
body:
Adds optional MON/workbench tools above frozen STR8N-F v0.3.0 BASE1/PR05. MON A/B g8 provides Dump/Modify, guarded force writes, bank prompts, TIME and recovery return. Services g4, WB2 g5 and PROGRAM/SP1 add maps/wear, board-loaded CLOCK/MAINT, flash/PROGRAM Table/Store/AUTO/Restore, compatible APPS and bounded BATCH. The MAINT LOAD option is consumed before dispatching bare MAINT.

Validation:
- 2609/65C816 emulation: physical MON B boot and installed CLOCK, forced reload, maps/wear, APPS inventory, Table and bounded BATCH passed. The later positive SS1 PROGRAM trial passed Store/AUTO, same-name versions, full-directory refusal, exact Restore, run/public-HOLD return and CRC refusal before copying RAM.
- That PROGRAM trial restored all 131072 SRAM bytes, all flash hashes and owner RAM/ZP; boot settings/history were unchanged. Two host-only handshake/acknowledgement errors and preserving continuations are retained in the acceptance evidence. Zero flash/journal/WORKSPACE/RTC-setting writes or power cuts.
- 2512/65C02 retains earlier monitor acceptance and positive PROGRAM/APPS RAM evidence with services g3. Current services g4 on 65C02 is not yet retested; 816 flash AP/02 owner-app launch is not claimed.
- The original five-sector install and separate D/E repair total seven erases, zero F writes/C erases; old D is archived and all pre-repair C records retained. RTC/NTP admission and historical samples remain intact.
- Published preview 1 extraction passed manifests, frozen F, terminal dependencies/help and ZIP checks. It includes the original Python terminal and unchanged foundation kit. Later PROGRAM evidence applies to the same binaries and does not replace those published archives.

ASM/DBG is deferred follow-on work and does not block the current scoped MON/tools release. The imported source is reference-only; the port is not execution-qualified. Full b35 parity, advanced CLOCK/FLASH/CONFIG and full BATCH coverage remain open. Published F, release tags and existing downloads stay unchanged.

Manual: docs/MON_FEATURE_PREVIEW.md
Installed acceptance: docs/2609_MON_FEATURE_ACCEPTANCE.md
Positive PROGRAM: docs/2609_PROGRAM_POSITIVE_ACCEPTANCE.md
Release scope: docs/FOUNDATION_RELEASE_PATH.md

title: Promote published STR8N-F 0.3.0 foundation and user documentation to main
body:
The public repository landing page still describes 0.2.0 while v0.3.0 and its operator/source downloads are already published. Promote the released BASE1 source, Python serial terminal, migration tools, user manual and scoped hardware evidence to main.

The README now says “4KB of firmware. One board. Up to four boot environments.” The adjacent explanation states that compatible user-supplied images run one at a time on shared CPU, RAM and peripherals. Main is the current release/integration branch; Mona and future ABI changes use feature branches. The immutable v0.3.0 tag and published ZIPs stay unchanged.

Validation: frozen-F/component/source/host integrity passed; prior package extraction and exact rc1 runtime equivalence receipts are included. Reviewed 2512 hardware cases and the 2609 extracted-rc1 existing-SNBT upgrade retain their original scopes. No new build, simulation or board access. F remains exactly 4096 bytes, SHA-256 8f4d35ac66730daa773515980983fcf442be3b1bdf1e523d3752ec3615657cc1. Final-package live trials and the WDC/programmer-F package routes remain NOT RUN.

The current main 0.2.0 tree was verified identical to the 0.2.0 baseline already in this branch. A history-only merge reconciles that squash without changing the reviewed release tree.

title: Release STR8N-F 0.2.0 boot and recovery toolkit
body:
Make STR8N-F the focused boot/recovery product with an operator ZIP and a separate complete source ZIP. The kit supplies the exact existing b15 F, CONFIG/OPAQUE/DEMO/READBACK RAM tools, optional BASE monitors, explicit component destinations, packet preparation and a quick start. Optional full-system components remain in the source package; the future SPI WORK journal and factory migration are outside the release.

Firmware bytes and the SNBT contract are unchanged. Preserve the b15/PR04/8000000F identity and document the USB hardware evidence and raw-loader limits. CI defaults to archive/source integrity; CPU models are manual opt-in.

Validation: 19 operator-kit files and 143 public source files checked after extraction; all committed public blobs match the source ZIP; payload hashes match their existing baselines. No assembly build, CPU-model rerun, board flashing or 2205 modification was performed. Private owner/WDC/SRAM/RTC captures are excluded.
